note: The current zoological-collections table records 41,000 Van der Horst histology slides of embryological material, mainly chordate and mammalian vertebrate. It separately reports complete card-catalogue documentation, about 60% computer-database coverage and some field notes. The museum history describes the research collection as built under Professors Van der Horst and Balinsky and as exceeding 40,000 embryological histology slides. The 41,000 figure is retained as the current institutional collection state rather than back-projected as a historical production total.

title: Classics revisited: C. J. van der Horst on pregnancy and menstruation in elephant shrews
citation: A. M. Carter, “Classics revisited: C. J. van der Horst on pregnancy and menstruation in elephant shrews,” Placenta 67 (2018): 24–30. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.placenta.2018.05.010
tags: South Africa; Wits; C. J. van der Horst; elephant shrew; embryology; placentation; histology slides; collection afterlife; Wisconsin
note: Carter reconstructs Van der Horst’s reproductive and placental research through the continuing evidentiary value of his collection. The paper explicitly acknowledges access to Van der Horst slides curated as part of the Harland W. Mossman Embryological Collection at the University of Wisconsin Zoological Museum. This establishes a trans-institutional slide afterlife, but it does not state how many Wits slides reached Wisconsin or whether the Wisconsin material is an original transferred subset, duplicates, or another preparation relationship; those provenance details remain open.

title: Harland Mossman Zoological Collection

tags: United States; Wisconsin; zoological museum; Harland W. Mossman; microscope slides; reproductive anatomy; embryology; research collection
note: UW–Madison identifies the Harland Mossman Zoological Collection as a research collection of microscope slides and preserved anatomical materials, especially vertebrate reproductive systems, for which the Zoological Museum is the repository. The institutional page does not identify a total slide count or a Van der Horst subset. The Van der Horst connection is therefore supplied only by Carter’s 2018 research article and is not silently imported into the museum’s own catalogue description.
